questions.heading: The Size-Limited License Stops at 2,000 Variables or 2,000 Rows
questions.stem: With only the size-limited license, a team builds a model of 1,500 variables and 2,300 rows. At which step does Gurobi refuse it?

options.text: At optimize(), which raises error 10010; building it works
options.says: Right: size_limit.py built 2,001 rows without complaint, and optimize() raised GurobiError 10010.

options.text: At addConstrs(), which refuses the 2,001st row as it is added
options.says: The rows were added and counted (NumConstrs 2,001) before the solve refused them.

options.text: At no step, since the limit counts variables and not rows
options.says: One variable with 2,001 rows was refused with error 10010 too.

options.text: At Env.start(), which checks every model's size in advance
options.says: start() reads the license before any model exists; the size is checked at optimize().

questions.heading: Four Kinds of License, and Where Each Can Run
questions.stem: A research group wants to run Gurobi jobs in containers on AWS Batch with Fargate. One member has an academic named-user license. Can the jobs use it?

options.text: Yes, if the license file is copied into the container image
options.says: A named-user license does not work in containers at all, and no license belongs in an image.

options.text: No, since containers need a WLS key or a license server instead
options.says: Right: the academic licensing article says named-user licenses cannot be used in containers; WLS can.

options.text: Yes, since Fargate containers run with no license checks
options.says: Running in a container does not remove licensing; Gurobi still needs a license, WLS or a server.

options.text: Yes, if GRB_LICENSE_FILE is set in the image's Dockerfile
options.says: GRB_LICENSE_FILE only names a file; a named-user license still does not work in a container.

questions.heading: Gurobi's Messages Can Name You; Mask Them
questions.stem: A planning API starts a Gurobi environment with OutputFlag=0 and, when Env.start() raises GurobiError, returns str(error) to the caller. What is wrong with that?

options.text: Nothing, since Gurobi's errors hold only an error code and a reason
options.says: The no-license error names the user, the host, a host id and the core count; the page shows it masked.

options.text: Nothing, since OutputFlag=0 strips such details from the errors
options.says: OutputFlag=0 silences the banner and the log; the error text still carries them, so it needs mask.

options.text: The caller gets no reason, since str(error) holds only the number
options.says: str(error) is the message itself, e.g. 'No Gurobi license found (...)'; the number is error.errno.

options.text: The text can name the user and the host, so mask it first
options.says: Right: license errors name the user and host; every message goes through mask before it leaves the program.
